pregunta: According to the ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765 definition cited in the text, Software Engineering includes which of the following elements?

opciones.texto: The application of a systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approach to software
The operation of software
The maintenance of software
The marketing of software products
The study of the approaches described above
The management of a company's IT budget

opciones.texto: Waterfall
Kanban
DevOps

Spiral

Requirements
Design

pregunta: Which statements about Kanban WIP (work-in-progress) limits are accurate according to the text?

opciones.texto: They constrain the number of tasks allowed in "doing" columns
They are normally set higher than the number of team members
They can help reveal an overwhelmed team
They are unrelated to identifying dormant tasks
They are normally set to less than or equal to the number of team members
They apply only to the "to do" column

pregunta: Which of the following are explicitly mentioned as reasons a feedback-based (agile) approach might be preferred over a plan-based one?

opciones.texto: The problem has significant unknowns
The business context is highly dynamic
The domain is subject to strict government regulation
The team wants to trade efficiency for adaptability
Life-or-death consequences of software errors must be minimized
The team wants to reduce uncertainty gradually as the project progresses

pregunta: According to the text, what can happen at the "Deployment" stage if anomalous behaviour (e.g., CPU load, memory usage) is detected after release?

opciones.texto: The system should immediately be shut down permanently
A roll-back to the previously deployed version must be triggered
The requirements stage must be restarted from scratch
The anomaly should be compared against the previous version's behaviour
The client must be notified before any technical action is taken
Monitoring should continue over the initial hours or days after release

pregunta: Which of the following are listed in the chapter as recommended "micro-level" work environment practices?

opciones.texto: Adopt a modern version management system such as git
Merge small, merge many, merge often
Avoid automation to retain manual control over releases
Adopt a branching naming convention traceable to ticket IDs
Keep the main trunk green (ready to deploy at all times)
Delay reverting a broken build until the next working day

pregunta: In the traceability matrix example (Table 1.1) for requirement FR#45, which of the following are true?

opciones.texto: The requirement involves both a front-end and a back-end container
Only one component is involved in total
An existing file had to be modified to support the new functionality
A graphical asset file is included among the associated files
The requirement involves exactly one file per component
Multiple components exist within the back-end container alone

pregunta: Which of the following does the text identify as things that should be monitored or checked during a software system's operational/maintenance phase?

opciones.texto: CPU, memory, and bandwidth usage
Normal users' activity
Attempted logins and denial-of-service attempts
The personal productivity of individual developers
Anomalies relative to the previously deployed version
The system's original ideation-stage business case

pregunta: Which of the following practices are associated in the text with the "Construction" stage specifically (as opposed to Integration or System testing)?

opciones.texto: Test-driven development (writing tests before code)
Testing components together with external dependencies like a database
Requesting a peer review before a component is integrated
Verifying non-functional requirements such as performance
Checking test coverage of the code written
Using test doubles to mimic external dependencies

pregunta: [W3] According to the text, which statements about a "baseline" are correct?

opciones.texto: It is a snapshot of one version of each artefact in the repository at a given point in time.
It can be changed freely by any team member without any approval process.
In practice, it often refers to a specific released version of the whole product after integration.
Baselines are only relevant to legal contracts, not to software artefacts.
A release is composed of a set of individually baselined files from the repository.
Modern Version Control Systems can list the set of versioned files tied to a specific release.

pregunta: [W3] Which of the following are core problems that Configuration Management tries to address, per the text?

opciones.texto: Simultaneous update, where the last save overwrites a teammate's previous work.
Limited notification, where a shared artefact changes but not everyone is told.
Managing multiple versions of the same file across production, testing and development.
Deciding which programming language the team should adopt.
Slow compilation times during the build process.
Propagating a defect fix across the different versions in which it appears.

pregunta: [W3] Since git is a distributed VCS, which of these statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Each team member holds a full local copy of the repository and its history.
Once pushed, commits become visible to other team members through the shared repository.
Uncommitted local changes are automatically shared the next time any teammate pulls.
If a workstation fails, the project history can still be recovered as long as one other copy of the repository exists.
A unique commit history that was never pushed can be permanently lost if that workstation is lost.
git requires a central server in order to store any project history at all.

pregunta: [W3] Which commands belong to the very simple local workflow described (create file, check status, stage, commit, verify)?

opciones.texto: git status
git add newfile.txt
git commit -m "message"
git push
git branch
git log

pregunta: [W3] Regarding git branching, which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Branching lets teams create independent versions of the repository for simultaneous development.
Finished work on a branch is typically merged back into the branch it originated from, e.g. the main trunk.
Two different developers can never work on the same branch at the same time.
A new branch can be created with git branch and navigated to with git checkout.
A feature branch can be deleted after it has been successfully merged.
Branching removes any need for communication between developers working on the same functionality.

pregunta: [W3] About trunk-based development, which of the following are correct?

opciones.texto: Teams merge back into the main/trunk branch simply and frequently, several times per hour.
It requires trusted, mature teams because every member can break production.
Feature toggles (flags) are often used to hide incomplete features from the deployed version.
It is the preferred approach for projects with complex, long-to-develop features needing separate branches.
If a merge breaks the main branch, it must be reverted immediately.
It is described as the only workflow that fully embraces continuous integration and delivery.

pregunta: [W3] About feature branching, which of the following are correct?

opciones.texto: Separate branches are created so multiple features or tasks can be worked on simultaneously.
Each feature branch is developed and tested in isolation from the main branch.
Gitflow and GitHub Flow are cited as popular workflows that incorporate feature branching.
Well-defined interfaces among functionalities help minimize conflicts when merging long-lived branches.
Feature branching guarantees zero integration conflicts, regardless of the application's structure.
Feature branching, not trunk-based development, is described as fully embracing continuous integration and delivery.

pregunta: [W3] Which descriptions of git commands match how they are presented in the text?

opciones.texto: git fetch --all retrieves information about all branches that exist in the remote shared repository.
git checkout is used to navigate onto an existing branch.
git merge integrates the changes of one branch into another, e.g. a feature branch into main.
git pull is used to synchronize a local branch with remote changes before pushing.
git commit sends local commits directly to teammates' machines, bypassing any shared repository.
git branch -d is used to delete a branch, e.g. after it has been merged.

pregunta: [W3] Regarding commit message conventions, which of the following are correct?

opciones.texto: When a ticketing system is used, the ticket ID should appear at the start of the commit message.
Conventional Commits is one proposed standard, but teams may agree on their own convention instead.
The "!" marker must always be included in the type field, whether or not the change is breaking.
Scripts can scan commit messages to check compliance with the agreed format.
LLMs can summarize the output of git diff --cached into a suggested commit message.
Once adopted, a commit convention should be kept undocumented so it stays flexible.

pregunta: [W3] Regarding repository structure and file naming, which of the following are correct?

opciones.texto: The proposed filename format is {project_name}_{discipline}_{description}-v{M.n}.extension.
The field separator is always an underscore, while a hyphen separates words within a field.
Source code files must follow this exact same filename convention.
The DEV folder's structure should reflect the software architecture and detailed design as closely as possible.
Every folder must contain a root README.md, except the top-level folder, which serves a different purpose.
The REQ folder's CRM subfolder records change requests to requirements along with the rationale for each decision.

pregunta: [W4] The project management iron triangle (Section 4.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Scope, resources and schedule are the vertices of the triangle, with quality at its centre.
Delivering all features on schedule may increase costs, e.g. by hiring additional staff.
Under stress, a project can be delivered with all features, on time and within budget, and still achieve great quality.
Delivering on time and within budget means some features will have to be dropped.
Staying within budget while delivering all features may lead to late delivery.
Under stress, quality is the element that is protected at all costs.

pregunta: [W4] Sprint burn-down charts and tables (Section 4.3.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The chart depicts the estimated remaining effort until the end of the sprint.
The assignee of each task updates the estimated remaining time at the end of every working day.
The remaining estimate of a task can never be higher than on the previous day if work was performed.
The burn-down records the actual effort, which is the measure used to predict completion.
Actual effort should still be recorded, but its goal is to improve future estimates.
A Release Burn-down tracks user stories or requirements on a timeline based on sprints, not days.

pregunta: [W4] Gantt charts (Section 4.3.2). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: They show a task list on the left and a timeline (days, weeks or months) on the horizontal axis.
Task bars show duration through their length and start/finish through their position on the timeline.
Dependencies between tasks are shown by arrows or lines and help to understand the critical path.
Milestones are significant points, often drawn as diamond-shaped markers.
A limitation is that they make it hard to flag whether the project as a whole is on time.
Some agile teams use them loosely as a roadmap preview of longer-term goals.

pregunta: [W4] Earned-value charts (Section 4.3.3). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Earned Value (EV), also called BCWP, is the value of the work actually completed by a point in time.
In agile contexts, Actual Cost (AC) corresponds to the estimated effort.
Planned Value (PV) is also known as Budgeted Cost of Work Scheduled (BCWS).
In agile contexts, PV is the sum of the actual effort of all tasks executed per sprint.
The approach is more adequate for agile projects than for plan-based projects.
Earned-value charts do not show the efficiency of the effort put into the work.

pregunta: [W4] Estimation techniques (Sections 4.4.1 to 4.4.3). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: In Wideband Delphi, members estimate individually, reveal together, and extreme estimators explain their rationale.
Planning Poker uses cards with Fibonacci-sequence points.
Planning Poker works best with absolute estimates in hours rather than relative estimates.
Cards above 20 or 40 are recommended for large tasks, so they need not be broken down.
When using informal heuristics, the team should record the assumptions behind the estimates.
Humans are better at comparing effort than at assigning absolute values, so relative estimates are preferred.

pregunta: [W4] Function points and the Cone of Uncertainty (Sections 4.4.4 and 4.4.5). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Function points measure functionality from the user's perspective, independently of technology.
Function point inputs include External Inputs, External Outputs, External Inquiries, Internal Logical Files and External Interface Files.
Function points are well suited to estimate managerial, non-technical tasks.
COCOMO is a detailed analytic approach that is seldom used in Agile settings.
The Cone of Uncertainty says estimation errors start very large and decrease as the project advances.
The initial error margin should be set at about 5% of the estimate.

pregunta: [W4] Risk identification (Section 4.5.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: It is the most difficult part of risk management, because it involves identifying unknowns.
An open atmosphere where people feel safe to raise issues helps reveal risks.
The SEI Risk Taxonomy-Based Questionnaire can serve as a starting point for a list of risks.
In the Fact Consequence format, the "fact" is something that may happen in the future.
The word "if" is forbidden in risk statements, to avoid risk hypochondria.
"The collapse of civilization can have an impact on our project" is the ideal, actionable risk statement.

pregunta: [W4] Risk analysis (Section 4.5.2). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The Threshold-of-Success (ToS) is the bare minimum achievement criteria that must all be met for success.
A ToS should be limited to roughly 3 to 5 items.
An odd number of likelihood/impact categories is recommended, to allow a neutral middle option.
Exact numeric probability and impact figures must always be assigned to every risk.
The risk matrix, with likelihood on one axis and impact on the other, is the input to risk planning.
ToS goals should be kept deliberately vague so that they remain flexible.

pregunta: [W4] Risk planning, monitoring and conclusions (Sections 4.5.3 to 4.6). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: "Avoid" aims to reduce the impact of the consequence if the risk occurs.
"Accept" means ignoring the risk completely, with no action at all.
"Mitigate" aims to remove the root cause of the risk.
Risk mitigation tasks should become a major part of the project effort.
Once a risk becomes a problem, it remains in the scope of risk management.
The risk matrix is static, so it never needs to be updated after it is drawn.

pregunta: [W5] Testing defined (Section 8.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Testing involves exercising software with concrete inputs and checking the output for correctness.
Testing ensures the absence of errors in a codebase.
Testing increases our trust in the codebase, which has value in and of itself.
Testing is the same as debugging, i.e. identifying where the defect is and correcting it.
The tester identifies the circumstances that trigger a defect; ideally the developer then debugs and fixes it.
The effort to maintain a codebase grows exponentially with its size, but only linearly when comprehensive tests are in place.

pregunta: [W5] Test cases, tests as code and the AAA structure (Sections 8.1 and 8.2). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: "Check login with valid password" is a very concrete scenario, thus serves as a good test specification.
A scenario with a specific username and password and a specified expected result is a correctly specified test case.
Expressing tests as code lets us re-run them after a fix or change and opens the way to CI/CD automation.
Tests-as-code do not need to follow any agreed format.
In the AAA style, the Assert step prepares the SUT to be exercised.
An optional fourth step, Clean-up, may be needed to restore the state of an external entity such as a database.

pregunta: [W5] Test selection and boundary value testing (Sections 8.3 and 8.3.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Exhaustive testing cannot be achieved even for a trivial program, because the set of inputs is virtually infinite.
A redundant test, or one that checks nothing relevant, is dead weight that must be maintained.
Boundary value testing uses only the minimum and maximum values of an input.
Boundary value testing rests on the observation that errors tend to cluster at the boundaries of inputs.
Boundary value testing is well suited to enumerated variables such as booleans.
Its effectiveness is independent of how well the component under test has been specified.

pregunta: [W5] Equivalence partitioning, state-transition and black-box testing (Sections 8.3.2 and 8.3.3). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Equivalence class partitioning divides the input data into classes that lead to equivalent results.
The goal is to reduce repeated tests while ensuring that each output partition is tested at least once.
Invalid inputs cannot lead to different output partitions.
State-transition testing evaluates behaviour as the application moves between states, e.g. whether a required sequence is followed.
These techniques are classified as black-box, as they ignore the internal structure of the source code.
Data-driven testing is always a black-box technique.

pregunta: [W5] LLM support in unit testing (Section 8.4). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: If the source code exists, it should be provided to the LLM as context together with a request to generate tests.
LLMs can help generate edge cases, create tests in a specific framework and update tests when the code changes.
A single generic prompt is enough: there is no need to specify the language or framework, or to iterate.
Without source code (test-first), a natural-language description or the function signature can be provided.
An LLM cannot generate tests unless the implementation already exists.
White-box tests should be favoured over black-box tests because they are more resilient to code changes.

pregunta: [W5] Testing and complexity management (Section 8.5). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Striving for testability enforces high modularity, otherwise tests would be unmanageably long and complex.
It is simpler to prepare a small module for testing (the Arrange step) than a large one.
Thinking about how to test a feature naturally leads us to group related concepts into cohesive modules.
Designing simple and fast tests pushes us to avoid dependencies, i.e. to reduce coupling.
Low coupling and high cohesion are achieved through separation of concerns ("one class, one thing, one method, one thing").
A testing mindset is fractal: it looks for coherence at each layer of abstraction.

pregunta: [W5] The testing pyramid: test levels (Section 8.6). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Unit tests form the base of the pyramid and should be the major number of tests (around 70% or more).
Unit tests target functionality with no external dependencies, so hundreds or thousands can run within seconds.
Integration tests validate interactions and interfaces between components, including external dependencies (around 20% or less).
System tests are also where quality attributes such as performance, scalability and stress are checked.
System tests are cheap and stable, so as many as possible should be automated.
A test of a unit that depends on other software units cannot be considered a unit test.

pregunta: [W5] The testing pyramid: rationale and the ice-cream antipattern (Section 8.6). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The ice-cream antipattern means having many unit tests and only a few system tests.
The pyramid promotes a small foundation of unit tests topped by many system tests.
In the ice-cream antipattern, locating a defect takes about the same effort as with a unit test.
System tests are not flaky, because the availability of the whole system makes them stable.
Acceptance tests are automated tests that form the base of the testing pyramid.
For system tests, the sensible strategy is to automate every possible end-user interaction.

pregunta: [W5] Other categories of tests (Section 8.6). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Acceptance tests are manual tests, normally performed by the client or end-users, and fall outside the testing pyramid.
User Acceptance Testing is automated and performed before the system tests.
A/B testing compares versions of a component by randomly splitting accesses; it needs a deployed application.
Exploratory testing involves manually exploring the software without a predefined test plan or script.
"Functional testing" is a term used only for acceptance tests.
Exploratory testing requires a predefined script so that results are reproducible.

pregunta: [W5] Test doubles and the chapter conclusions (Sections 8.7 and 8.8). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Test doubles are code that replaces and emulates the behaviour of other parts of the code.
They are typically used to replace external dependencies that are slow or lead to flaky tests.
They can stand in for dependencies that are not yet available, e.g. in a top-to-bottom construction plan.
A test mock mimics dynamic behaviour, allowing verification of how a component interacts with its dependency.
A test stub returns a predetermined value, and the tests of the dependent component need to be aware of it.
Using test doubles turns unit tests into integration tests.

pregunta: [W6] Automation: motivation and scope (chapter introduction). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Running a test manually may be acceptable once or twice, but it soon becomes unfeasible and error-prone.
Test automation exempts us from writing the tests in the first place.
As the codebase grows and more tests are added, the effort of running them remains the same: just start a script.
Automation is limited to running tests; other tasks must still be done by hand.
Any service available as a command can be triggered by an automation script (compiling, syntax checking, deploying, messaging developers...).
Reducing the test effort increases the likelihood of identifying defects early, ideally right after they are introduced.

pregunta: [W6] Basics of GitLab CI: the .gitlab-ci.yml file and runners (Section 10.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The automation script is stored in the .gitlab-ci.yml file in the project root folder.
By default, the jobs run on the developer's own local machine.
The commands in the script are the same ones we would run on the command line (echo, date, pwd...).
By default, the jobs run in GitLab-hosted Docker containers: think of a freshly installed machine.
With no trigger criteria defined, the script runs whenever a new commit is made visible in the GitLab instance via a git push.
Committing only in your local machine is enough to trigger the pipeline.

pregunta: [W6] Defining the environment of a test job (Section 10.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: "image: python" is needed because the default Docker image in GitLab is Ruby.
A "pip install -r requirements.txt" command is needed in the script because the runner is a fresh environment without your dependencies.
If no image is specified, GitLab uses a Python image by default.
The before_script keyword defines additional setup tasks that run before the remaining script.
With unittest, "python -m unittest discover dir/" discovers all the test files in a folder, so they need not be called one by one.
The runner reuses the Python packages already installed on your machine.

pregunta: [W6] Stages and jobs (Section 10.1.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: Jobs in the same stage run in parallel, so a priori no specific execution order can be assumed among them.
Jobs in later stages wait until all jobs in the preceding stages terminate.
The straightforward way to impose an execution order between two jobs is to put them in the same stage.
Jobs of the same stage always run one at a time, in the order in which they are written.
The keyword "needs" can be used to make jobs start earlier than the stage ordering would allow.
A pipeline must have exactly four stages: Static Analysis, Test, Security and Deploy.

pregunta: [W6] Triggers, failures and good practices in job definition (Section 10.1.2). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: With "only: merge_requests", the linting and complexity jobs (in the example of the chapter) are activated only on merge requests.
A script can only be triggered by a commit; other events are not supported.
By default, a failed job aborts the pipeline, so the following stages are never executed.
"allow_failure: true" lets the pipeline continue; the stage is marked as "passed with warnings".
Good practice is to place all commands in a single job to keep the file short.
Passwords should be written directly in the script so that every runner can find them.

pregunta: [W6] Static analysis tools, coverage and artifacts (Sections 10.1.2 and 10.1.3). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: When the pipeline terminates, its dedicated environment is discarded and all data in it is lost.
The "artifacts:" keyword instructs GitLab CI to store specified files after the job finishes.
Artifacts are stored in the original repository, e.g. in the ./my-tests folder.
Running "coverage xml" generates a Cobertura-compatible XML test coverage report.
pylint is the tool used in the example to compute cyclomatic complexity and the maintainability index.
radon is a Python tool that computes metrics such as cyclomatic complexity, maintainability index and Halstead metrics.

pregunta: [W6] Rules, manual jobs and deploy scripts (Section 10.1.4). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The "rules" keyword can restrict a job to certain branches, e.g. only main and staging.
In the example, the security checks are only performed on feature branches.
When a job's rule is not satisfied, the pipeline simply skips it and moves on to the next stage.
"when: manual" keeps the pipeline waiting for an explicit trigger in the GitLab UI, useful for a final human check before deployment.
The deploy commands must be written inline in .gitlab-ci.yml; calling a separate shell script is not possible.
Only the commands pre-installed by GitLab can be run in a job.

pregunta: [W6] Automation tool versus the commands it runs (end of Section 10.1). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The CI tool reads the automation file, creates the environment(s) and orchestrates the pipeline stages.
The hierarchy is: pipeline stages contain named jobs, which contain the specific commands to execute.
pytest, coverage and bandit are examples of automation tools, like GitLab CI.
Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Travis CI and Atlassian Bamboo are other automation tools.
CI/CD syntaxes are grouped in three families: procedural, declarative and functional.
Pipeline visual displays are read-only: jobs cannot be replayed or triggered from them.

pregunta: [W6] Benefits and reach of automation (Section 10.2). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: The developer creates application code for the client's requirements but also automation code that supports their own development tasks.
Automation scripts are created, managed and shared by the whole team, not by each developer individually.
Libraries of automation scripts are rare, so each project has to write its own from scratch.
Automation can generate reports that give evidence for decision making, e.g. early identification of quality and progress issues.
Automation is limited to the developer's own machine.
Continuous Practices is the name given to CI/CD because it can include integration, documentation, delivery, deployment, certification, monitoring and more.

pregunta: [W6] LLM support for writing and debugging automation scripts (Section 10.3). Which statements are correct?

opciones.texto: LLMs can help from creating templates to debugging issues in automation scripts.
LLM support is limited to GitLab; other tools such as GitHub Actions or Jenkins are not covered.
LLMs can analyse and describe a provided script, and spot wrong indentation, misplaced keys, missing dependencies or shell command typos.
LLM output can be accepted as is, because errors in pipelines are easier to spot than in source code.
Errors latent in a pipeline can be more insidious and harder to spot than errors in source code, so proceed step by step and test thoroughly.
LLMs can suggest best practices such as job caching, secrets management, parallelization and proper use of job dependencies or needs.
